clue.text: To reduce babysitting commitments is mad

definitions.meaning: to look after children (mind them) less often, read as two words

explanation.surface: Someone declares that cutting back on babysitting duties would be crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is a whimsical split: MIND (babysit) plus LESS, i.e. do less minding.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone acting without reason or sense is crazy, a straightforward synonym for mad.

clue.text: 1-0 for United

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
zero is none, nothing at all

explanation.surface: A football scoreline of one-nil for a team called United.
explanation.walkthrough: 'United' looks like the name of a football club, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Things joined together into a single whole are combined, as the phrase means.

clue.text: Kisses are deceptive?

parts.note: kisses are written as a pair of crosses at the foot of a letter, and a kiss can be treacherous, like Judas's

explanation.surface: A wry question about whether kisses can be misleading.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair of X marks is literally two crosses, and the phrase also means to betray.

clue.text: Joining battle and winning

definitions.meaning: an army engages the enemy when it starts fighting
winning in the sense of charming and attractive

explanation.surface: Taking part in a fight and coming out on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Armies engage when they begin fighting; and a winning smile is a charming, attractive one.

clue.text: Reduction in extra earnings supported by miners' leader and deputy

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece above is supported by what follows below it
reduction signals the word is shortened by its final letter

parts.note: money from a second job is a second income

indicators.note: leader points to the opening letter of the word miners'

explanation.surface: A cut in overtime pay is backed by the miners' union chief and his deputy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reduction in' trims SECOND INCOME to SECOND INCOM; 'supported by' puts M and AND beneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: A deputy is the person next in rank who takes charge when the chief is absent.

clue.text: Adding to cape, trace unknown fabric

parts.note: C is the map abbreviation for cape
a hint is a trace or slight suggestion
Z is one of the algebraic letters standing for an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: A tailor adds to a cape some unidentified fabric, with a trace of it showing.
explanation.definitionFit: Chintz is a glazed printed cotton, a kind of fabric used for curtains and upholstery.

clue.text: Firm endlessly exploiting family member

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: endlessly means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: using someone is exploiting them

explanation.surface: A company keeps exploiting a relative.
explanation.definitionFit: A cousin is a relative, the child of one's aunt or uncle.

clue.text: Bug installed in their kitchen

indicators.note: installed in signals a word sitting within the run of letters

explanation.surface: An insect has taken up residence in someone's kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bug' suggests an insect or a listening device; it is the verb meaning annoy.
explanation.definitionFit: To bug someone is to annoy them, the same as to irritate.

clue.text: Thanks to one person advancing, I'm likely to be behind

parts.note: ta is informal British for thanks
I is the Roman numeral for one
a lender advances money to others

explanation.surface: Thanks to someone getting ahead, I expect to fall behind.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the poorer batsmen bat last, at the end of the order, so such a player is behind the others.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricketer batting at the bottom of the order comes in behind the rest of the team.

clue.text: Corn and chopped egg on bread

parts.note: a cob is the head of maize, corn on the cob

indicators.note: chopped means cut short, so the final letter goes

parts.note: to egg someone on is to urge them

explanation.surface: A recipe: corn with chopped egg served on toast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egg' looks like food here, but 'egg on' is a verb phrase meaning urge.
explanation.definitionFit: A coburg is a round crusty loaf with a cross cut in its top, a type of bread.

clue.text: Abandons cut of meat that's half burnt

parts.note: chuck is a cut of beef from the neck and shoulder

indicators.note: half signals keeping only the first three of six letters

parts.note: singed means lightly burnt

explanation.surface: A cook gives up on a joint of meat that has been half burnt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' keeps the first half of SINGED, giving SIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To chuck in a job is to give it up, so it is an informal synonym for abandons.

clue.text: Healthy source of water

definitions.meaning: a shaft sunk to draw water from the ground

explanation.surface: A spring of fresh water that is good for you.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in good health is being well; and a shaft dug for water is a classic water supply.

clue.text: Belligerent type, nasty foreign thug with nothing to lose

indicators.note: nasty signals the letters are roughed up into a new order

parts.note: O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: A violent foreign thug who has nothing to lose is a dangerous man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with nothing to lose' tells you an O is removed from FOREIGN THUG before 'nasty' rearranges the remaining letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A gunslinger who settles quarrels with shots is a combative, aggressive person.

clue.text: Drop litter? React with disapproval

definitions.meaning: a cat giving birth to a litter of young
to be very upset or agitated about something

explanation.surface: Someone frowns on people dropping rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'litter' looks like rubbish, but here it means a brood of young animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat bearing young literally does this; idiomatically the phrase means getting into a state of alarm.

clue.text: TV icon is revolutionary film director

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned over or overthrown, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A television star is said to be a radical film-maker.
explanation.definitionFit: Luchino Visconti was an Italian film-maker, director of The Leopard and Death in Venice.

clue.text: I am opposed to a line being made up

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm, written without the apostrophe
agin is dialect for against, opposed to
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: Someone declares opposition to a line being invented.
explanation.walkthrough: AGIN is an old dialect form of 'against'; RY is a standard abbreviation for railway.
explanation.definitionFit: Something invented or fictional exists only in the mind, as an unreal thing does.

clue.text: See red, ultimately entering struggle

indicators.note: entering means one piece goes inside another

parts.note: to vie is to compete or struggle

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the word red

explanation.surface: Someone sees red and enters into a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See red' looks like the idiom for anger, but 'See' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Vide is the Latin instruction used in texts to refer readers elsewhere, meaning look at.

clue.text: End up keeping girl in antacid mixture

indicators.note: keeping means holding something inside
in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: an aim is an end or goal
Agnes is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl ends up kept in a mixture for indigestion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns AIM into MIA, which then holds AGNES.
explanation.definitionFit: Milk of magnesia is a suspension taken to neutralise stomach acid.

clue.text: I work to secure Desdemona's end

definitions.text: I work to secure Desdemona's end

indicators.note: to secure means to hold something within, so one letter is enclosed

parts.note: to go is to work or function, as a machine does

indicators.note: end points to the final letter of the name Desdemona

explanation.surface: A villain boasts of working to bring about Desdemona's death.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's Othello the villain schemes so that Desdemona is killed; the whole clue is both the wordplay and his description.
explanation.definitionFit: The villain of Othello engineers the murder of Desdemona by her husband.

clue.text: Fine examples of fireworks

definitions.meaning: a cracker is informally an excellent example of something

explanation.surface: Some especially good specimens of fireworks.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally an excellent thing is a cracker; and crackers are bangers set off at festivals.

clue.text: Plundered centre of Uxbridge, then ran off

indicators.note: centre of points to the two middle letters of the town name

parts.note: fled means ran away

explanation.surface: Someone robbed the middle of Uxbridge then escaped.
explanation.walkthrough: Uxbridge is a town in west London; its centre is its fourth and fifth letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle a place is to search it in order to steal, to ransack or plunder it.

clue.text: Officer interfered with a PM and his mind

indicators.note: interfered with means tampered with, so the letters are disturbed

explanation.surface: Someone meddled with the Prime Minister and his thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: A midshipman is a junior naval officer rank.

clue.text: Jog to relax occasional tensions, principally

indicators.note: principally points to the leading letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Advice that a jog helps to ease occasional stress.
explanation.definitionFit: To trot is to run at a gentle pace, a synonym for jogging.

clue.text: Route winding over the top

indicators.note: winding means twisting about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A road twisting over the summit.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bizarre or unconventional is extreme, beyond normal bounds.

clue.text: Spoil beautiful Italian holiday resort

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or damage
bella is the Italian for beautiful

explanation.surface: A lovely Italian woman spoils a holiday at the resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Marbella is a Spanish seaside town on the Costa del Sol, popular with holidaymakers.

clue.text: Perhaps book about Darwin's scientific study

definitions.text: Perhaps book about Darwin's scientific study

parts.words: Perhaps book about Darwin's scientific study
parts.note: a life story of the naturalist, or short for the science of living things he studied

explanation.surface: A possible book on Darwin's research.
explanation.definitionFit: The short form serves both for a written life story and for the life science.

clue.text: Dealt with broadcast of drama's second part?

indicators.note: broadcast signals the words are spoken over the air

parts.note: the second section of a play's act would be its second scene

explanation.surface: Something was handled by broadcasting the second episode of a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drama's second part' read as SCENE TWO, which when spoken resembles the two-word phrase meaning handled.
explanation.definitionFit: If a matter has been attended to or handled, it has been dealt with.

clue.text: Single utterance from yours truly in radio quiz

definitions.text: Single utterance from yours truly in radio quiz

parts.words: Single utterance from yours truly in radio quiz
parts.note: yours truly is the speaker himself, so a single spoken term of his own; also the title of a long-running BBC radio panel game on words

explanation.surface: A contestant on a radio quiz speaks just one word.
explanation.walkthrough: My Word! was a BBC radio panel game about language; the phrase is also an exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both an exclamation of surprise and the name of a wordplay quiz on British radio.

clue.text: Pay careful attention, reversing across street in racing car

indicators.note: across means set over, so one piece spans another
reversing means the word for paying attention is read from right to left

parts.note: to regard is to pay close attention to

explanation.surface: A driver pays attention while reversing across the street in a racing car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversing' turns REGARD into DRAGER, and 'across' sets that around ST.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragster is a car built for drag racing over short straight tracks.
